intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card component that demonstrates essential web accessibility (a11y) practices. You will learn how to use semantic HTML elements, proper ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes, and keyboard navigation support to make your React applications usable for everyone. The core programming concepts involve structuring JSX with accessibility in mind and managing focus states using TypeScript. By the end, you'll understand how to apply fundamental a11y principles to create inclusive web interfaces in React with TypeScript.
intro.usecase: Accessibility fundamentals are essential in every production React application to ensure all users, including those with disabilities, can effectively interact with your interface. In real-world scenarios, developers implement a11y features in form validation systems to provide clear error messages for screen readers, in navigation menus with proper keyboard focus management, and in data tables with semantic HTML structure for assistive technologies. For example, an e-commerce checkout form needs aria-live regions for dynamic price updates, while a financial dashboard requires proper heading hierarchy and color contrast for users with visual impairments. These implementations are critical for compliance with WCAG standards and creating inclusive digital products that serve diverse user populations.
